LLM auditresponse for itgray-bin.install:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard pacman `.install` file that manages a privileged TUN helper for the ITG Ray application. The `_configure_uid` function writes a UID to `/etc/itgray/helper.env` to control which user can drive the helper, inferring the desktop user from `SUDO_UID` or the first regular account in `/etc/passwd`. All file operations are confined to the package's own directories (`/etc/itgray/`, `/run/itgray-helper.sock`), and the existing config file is never overwritten.

The post-install/upgrade/remove hooks perform routine systemd service management (daemon-reload, enable/disable, restart) and cleanup — all standard packaging practices. No network requests, no downloads, no obfuscated code, no eval, and no operations outside the application's scope.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard install hook for systemd helper configuration; no security issues.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices. The source tarball is fetched from the project's official GitHub releases URL (`github.com/IvanTopGaming/ITG_Ray`), and a sha256 checksum is provided (not SKIP). All file operations are conventional: copying app binaries into `/usr/lib/itgray`, creating hardlinks for helper binaries and cores (sing-box, xray) so they are resolvable as siblings of the executable, installing a systemd service, desktop file, and icon, and creating a standard shell wrapper in `/usr/bin`. Setting `chmod 4755` on `chrome-sandbox` is Electron's documented setuid sandbox helper mechanism used by many legitimate Electron applications. The package is a VPN client (VLESS/sing-box) with a privileged TUN helper, which inherently requires elevated permissions for network tunnel functionality — this is expected upstream behavior, not injected malicious code. No obfuscation, suspicious network calls, dangerous command usage (eval, base64, curl|bash), or anomalous file operations were detected.
</details>

<summary>Standard AUR PKGBUILD for VPN client, no issues found.</summary>
